name: Symbrachydactyly of Hands and Feet

criteria.description: Presence of shortened or absent digits on hands and/or feet
Fusion of adjacent digits (syndactyly) in affected limbs
Hypoplasia or absence of nails on affected digits
Radiographic evidence of absent or hypoplastic phalanges

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of digital shortening or absence combined with syndactyly and radiographic confirmation of phalangeal anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing is not routinely diagnostic.

imaging: Radiographs showing absent or hypoplastic phalanges and metacarpals/metatarsals
MRI may show soft tissue hypoplasia in affected digits
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; mostly sporadic cases
Rare familial cases reported with possible autosomal dominant inheritance
other: Clinical examination revealing digital shortening, syndactyly, and nail anomalies

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of localized skin absence rather than digital shortening
Complex syndactyly involving fusion of bones, not just soft tissue

redFlags: Severe functional impairment of hand or foot requiring early intervention
Presence of vascular anomalies suggesting limb ischemia
Associated developmental delay or neurological abnormalities
references: Temtamy SA, McKusick VA. The Genetics of Hand Malformations. Springer-Verlag, 1978.
Kozin SH. Congenital Hand Anomalies: Diagnosis and Management. J Am Acad Orthop Surg. 2010.
